Credit pic: ViTrox\n\nKUALA LUMPUR: Emerging supply constraints and a moderating growth momentum have prompted AmInvestment Bank to downgrade ViTrox Corporation Bhd to \"Hold\" from \"Buy\", despite the company registering 173 per cent surge in core profit in the first nine months.\n\nDespite the strong financial showing, AmInvestment analyst Paul Yap Ee Xing highlighted that growth momentum is expected to moderate as the company faces a high base effect.\n\nThe group's book-to-bill ratio has already eased from 1.5 times in the previous quarter to 1.1 times.\n\nManagement has guided fourth-quarter revenue to land between RM403 million and RM459 million. Its automated board inspection (ABI) backlog stands at a healthy RM399 million, offering revenue visibility into the first half of 2027.\n\nA pressing concern for the technology firm lies in emerging supply chain bottlenecks. Following a significant order pull-in during the third quarter, ViTrox had to draw down its inventory to meet near-term demand, leaving a tighter material buffer for upcoming quarters.\n\n\"AXI (automated X-ray inspection) equipment output is constrained by the supply of X-ray tubes.\n\n\"While the procurement and R&D teams are actively exploring alternative sources across different countries and suppliers, challenges remain in bridging gaps in pricing and technical specifications,\" said Yap in a note.\n\nThe automated vision inspection solutions provider reported a 9M 2026 core net profit of RM263 million, beating market consensus by coming in at 83 per cent of full-year estimates.\n\nA key catalyst for this robust performance was the deployment of AI infrastructure, which propelled communication-related revenue to 42 per cent of the group's total.\n\nViTrox's QX AXI equipment has been adopted as the standard by a major hyperscaler, single-handedly contributing 15 per cent to the group's revenue, noted AmInvestment.\n\nLooking forward, potential growth catalysts for ViTrox include advanced packaging and inspection solutions designed for next-generation AI accelerator boards and cold plates.\n\nAmInvestment is keeping its target price for ViTrox unchanged at RM10.25, which is based on a target price-to-earnings (PE) multiple of 40 times on blended 2027/28 earnings per share.\n\nGiven the current trajectory, the firm caution that upside surprises will become increasingly difficult for the company to deliver amidst tightening supply hurdles.","highlights":["November 10, 2026 @ 12:27am\n\nEmerging supply constraints and a moderating growth momentum have prompted AmInvestment Bank to downgrade ViTrox Corporation Bhd to “Hold” from “Buy”, despite the company registering 173 per cent surge in core profit in the first nine months. Corporation Berhad - AI Demand Drives a Third Record Quarter | I3investor\n\n### Vitrox Corporation Berhad - AI Demand Drives a Third Record Quarter \n\n Date: 2026-11-06 \n\nFirm: JF APEX Stock: VITROX Price Target: 14.44 Price Call: BUY Last Price: 10.22 Upside/Downside: +4.22 (41.29%)\n\n- VITROX posted a record 3QFY26 core net profit of RM121.4m (+253.0% YoY, +44.7% QoQ), exceeding both our expectations and consensus, lifting 9MFY26 core net profit to RM266.0m (+170.4% YoY), which came in at 96.5% of our previous FY26F forecast of RM275.6m and 83.9% of consensus.\n- We remain bullish on VITROX's earnings trajectory into FY27, underpinned by sustained AI data centre and HBM-related demand, accelerating edge AI device adoption and deepening advanced packaging penetration, alongside further margin expansion from operating leverage as shipment volumes continue to scale.\n- We raise our FY26F/FY27F/FY28F core net profit forecasts by 37.8%/23.4%/22.6% to RM379.7m/RM447.1m/RM500.4m, imputing higher ABI and MVS shipment and ASP assumptions, firmer margins and revised RM/USD assumptions.\n- Maintain BUY with a higher TP of RM14.44 (from RM11.12), based on the 5-year historical mean PE of 54.67x applied to rolled-over FY28F EPS of 26.4sen.\n\nAbove estimates. The Group's 3QFY26 core net profit of RM121.4m (+253.0% YoY, +44.7% QoQ) was arrived at after adding back an impairment loss on financial assets (RM2.3m) and net inventories written down (RM1.3m), and excluding a net forex gain (RM0.5m) and a net fair value gain on financial instruments (RM0.3m). This lifted 9MFY26 core net profit to RM266.0m (+170.4% YoY), at 96.5% of our previous FY26F forecast and 83.9% of consensus, driven by record ABI and MVS billings amid the AI-led semiconductor upcycle, a further step-up in operating margins and a lower effective tax rate under VTSB's MIDA pioneer incentive.\n\nQoQ. Revenue expanded 29.4% QoQ to a record RM485.1m (2QFY26: RM374.9m), driven by higher shipment deliveries and strong order fulfilment across both the ABI and MVS segments. PBT grew 36.8% QoQ to RM136.8m (2QFY26: RM99.9m) on favourable operating leverage from higher shipment volumes, with EBIT margin widening to a record 28.1% (2QFY26: 26.8%). Core net profit rose 44.7% QoQ to RM121.4m (2QFY26: RM83.9m), further aided by a lower effective tax rate of 13.7% (2QFY26: 15.5%).\n\nYoY. Revenue surged 112.2% YoY to RM485.1m as demand for advanced inspection solutions for AI infrastructure, networking equipment and HBM/advanced packaging accelerated across both segments. PBT jumped 171.0% YoY to RM136.8m on manufacturing economies of scale and a richer product mix, while core net profit rose 253.0% YoY to RM121.4m, with the EBIT margin expanding to 28.1% (3QFY25: 22.4%) and the effective tax rate falling to 13.7% (3QFY25: 32.0%, when VTSB's earlier pioneer status had lapsed before the new MIDA exemption was granted in 4QFY25). Core net profit margin improved to 25.0% (3QFY25: 15.0%).\n\nWorking capital build-up. Receivables rose 82.6% YTD to RM684.0m (end-FY25: RM374.5m) and inventories rose 76.5% to RM528.0m (end-FY25: RM299.2m), both outpacing the 67.0% increase in quarterly revenue from 4QFY25 to 3QFY26. The resulting RM288.9m working capital outflow, partly funded by higher payables (+RM213.0m), turned 9MFY26 operating cash flow negative at -RM8.5m (9MFY25: +RM101.5m) and lowered net cash to RM206.8m (end-FY25: RM316.6m). We view the build-up as largely a function of the shipment ramp rather than a sign of weakening collections, with contract liabilities more than doubling to RM73.3m (end-FY25: RM32.2m) pointing to a firm order pipeline.\n\nOutlook. We expect sustained AI data centre investment, accelerating edge AI device demand and the Group’s continued push into advanced packaging and HBM inspection solutions to support further earnings growth into FY27, with VTSB’s MIDA pioneer incentive (effective through September 2030) keeping the effective tax rate below the statutory rate. Management anticipates a favourable operating environment for the remainder of FY26 and into 2027, though it remains mindful of forex volatility and geopolitical risks to the semiconductor supply chain.\n\nEarnings Revision. Following the third consecutive record quarter, we raise our FY26F/FY27F/FY28F core net profit forecasts by 37.8%/23.4%/22.6% to RM379.7m/RM447.1m/RM500.4m (from RM275.6m/RM362.4m/RM408.2m), imputing higher ABI and MVS shipment and ASP assumptions, firmer margins and revised RM/USD assumptions of 4.03/4.15/4.15 (from 4.05/4.05/4.05), partly offset by a higher effective tax rate assumption of 15%/14%/14% (from 10%/8%/10%).\n\nValuation & Recommendation. We maintain our BUY rating with a higher TP of RM14.44 (from RM11.12), based on the 5-year historical mean PE of 54.67x applied to rolled over FY28F EPS of 26.4sen, backed by (i) accelerating AI-driven demand for advanced packaging and high-precision inspection, (ii) sustained double-digit earnings growth over our forecast horizon","highlights":["### Vitrox Corporation Berhad - AI Demand Drives a Third Record Quarter \n\n Date: 2026-11-06 \n\nFirm: JF APEX Stock: VITROX Price Target: 14.44 Price Call: BUY Last Price: 10.22 Upside/Downside: +4.22 (41.29%)\n\n- VITROX posted a record 3QFY26 core net profit of RM121.4m (+253.0% YoY, +44.7% QoQ), exceeding both our expectations and consensus, lifting 9MFY26 core net profit to RM266.0m (+170.4% YoY), which came in at 96.5% of our previous FY26F forecast of RM275.6m and 83.9% of consensus.\n- We remain bullish on VITROX's earnings trajectory into FY27, underpinned by sustained AI data centre and HBM-related demand, accelerating edge AI device adoption and deepening advanced packaging penetration, alongside further margin expansion from operating leverage as shipment volumes continue to scale.\n- We raise our FY26F/FY27F/FY28F core net profit forecasts by 37.8%/23.4%/22.6% to RM379.7m/RM447.1m/RM500.4m, imputing higher ABI and MVS shipment and ASP assumptions, firmer margins and revised RM/USD assumptions.\n- Maintain BUY with a higher TP of RM14.44 (from RM11.12), based on the 5-year historical mean PE of 54.67x applied to rolled-over FY28F EPS of 26.4sen.\n\n...\n\nQoQ. The exhibition will be held from 3 to 5 November 2026 at the Setia SPICE Convention Centre in Penang, Malaysia, where ViTrox will be exhibiting at Booth #2156.\n\nAs Automex Penang 2026 brings together manufacturers, engineers, and industry decision-makers to explore solutions that improve productivity and competitiveness, ViTrox is using this platform to present its latest innovations in digital manufacturing and intelligent automation. ViTrox will showcase a comprehensive portfolio of smart manufacturing solutions, including:\n\nV-ONE 5.0: The Industrial Data Intelligence Platform\n\nViTrox's V-ONE 5.0 forms the digital backbone of its Manufacturing Intelligence Solutions, driving manufacturers towards Industry 5.0. It unifies machines, enterprise systems, and human operations into one ecosystem, converting shop-floor data into real-time, actionable insights to optimise production efficiency and drive data-driven smart manufacturing.\n\nHighlighted V-ONE 5.0 Features\n\nV-ONE 5.0 An intuitive, low-code platform that is engineered to accelerate the development of custom Industry 4.0 applications with drag-and-drop tools. Powered by Builder AI, teams can describe what they need in a prompt and have it set up workflows and chatbots, auto-generate UI layouts, convert flowcharts into e-tickets and create live-data widgets, while the V-ONE Marketplace provides instant access to over 70 ready-to-use apps that proactively solve manufacturing challenges.\n\nV-ONE MARS An industry-grade gateway that simplifies data acquisition and logic automation through intuitive interfaces, enabling seamless sensor integration and real-time analytics. Powered by V-ONE MARS Edge software, it connects to the V-ONE Cloud via multiple interfaces and protocols, supporting zero-code IoT configuration through device components, function nodes, and logic workflows.\n\nDIMo – Tablet Version A flexible Job Intelligence solution developed for manufacturing environments, supporting both cloud and on-premise deployments. It digitalises work order management and production tracking while improving communication and coordination between planning teams and shop-floor operations through DIMo interactive devices.\n\nPrompt Support for Digital Analytics — An AI assistant that turns industrial data into clear, actionable insights through natural language interaction, enabling real-time troubleshooting and production analysis.\n\nMES & ERP Integration: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) acts as the organisation's strategic backbone, unifying core business functions such as finance, procurement, and sales to enable seamless, enterprise-wide data flow. Working in alignment with broader business objectives, the Manufacturing Execution System (MES) delivers real-time visibility and control over the production floor, converting high-level orders into precise, trackable operations that enhance shop-floor efficiency.\n\nV-Trace Solutions for End-to-End Manufacturing Traceability\n\nV-Trace Solutions provides intelligent process guidance and automated product verification to strengthen manufacturing accuracy, quality control, and traceability across production:\n\nVisionSmartGuide — An AI vision-powered solution that provides real-time guidance and step-by-step process validation for manual assembly operations. Using AI video processing technology helps error-proof assembly at the source by validating each step as it happens, flagging incorrectly assembled products before they proceed to the next stage.\n\nVisionSmartCheck — An automated vision inspection solution powered by the VisionXpert Smart Camera. Acting as a digital gatekeeper on the production line, it replaces subjective manual inspection with traceable automated verification while transferring inspection data to the V-Trace server for complete end-to-end traceability.\n\nVisionXpert: Intelligent Vision Solutions\n\nThe VisionXpert Solutions deliver edge-level vision processing that enables fast inspection, real-time decision-making, and seamless integration into smart manufacturing environments:\n\nVisionXpert Smart Camera (XC-330) An advanced smart vision solution engineered to deliver fast and accurate inspection with seamless integration into production environments. Equipped with a powerful built-in processor and a comprehensive suite of ready-to-use vision tools, the XC Series performs edge-level image processing directly at the source, reducing system latency while improving inspection accuracy, operational efficiency, and production reliability.\n\nVisionXpert Smart Code Reader (XS-130) Engineered to enha","highlights":["2nd November 2026 - ViTrox Showcases Intelligent Automation and Manufacturing Intelligence Solutions at Automex Penang 2026\n\nPENANG, MALAYSIA – October 2026 – ViTrox, which aims to be the World’s Most Trusted Technology Company, is pleased to announce its participation in Automex Penang 2026. Revenue was up more than 110% year-on-year to RM485.1 million.\n\nLooking ahead, ViTrox expects a favourable business environment for the remainder of the financial year and into 2027, supported by robust growth in the semiconductor sector, continued investment in data centre infrastructure and rising demand for edge artificial intelligence (AI) devices.\n\nThe company — which makes machines used to automatically inspect and detect defects in semiconductor components and printed circuit board assemblies — said it is seeking to capture a slice of the increasing complexity of AI accelerators and high bandwidth memory.\n\nNet profit in the first nine months of the year also jumped to RM254.8 million from RM87 million a year earlier, supported by sustained capital expenditure deployment from strong AI infrastructure demand and electronics manufacturing customers.\n\nRevenue for the period also more than doubled to RM1.13 billion from RM552.7 million.\n\n“The group will continue to exercise prudent cost management and operational discipline to mitigate potential risks from foreign exchange volatility and geopolitical uncertainties,” ViTrox said.\n\nNo interim dividend was declared for the quarter under review, though the company had paid out 1.18 sen per share in July.\n\nShares of ViTrox ended Thursday at RM10.60, down 30 sen or 2.8%, giving the Penang-based company a market capitalisation of RM20 billion ahead of the results announcement. \n\nThe content is a snapshot from Publisher. Contact us for any changes.","highlights":["KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 5): ViTrox Corporation Bhd (KL: VITROX) is upbeat after the semiconductor equipment maker posted its best quarter since listing in 2005, as higher volume drove down unit costs.\n\nNet profit for the three months ended Sept 30, 2026 (3QFY2026) was RM118.6 million, more than tripled from RM34.7 million a year earlier, according to an exchange filing. Revenue was up more than 110% year-on-year to RM485.1 million.\n\nLooking ahead, ViTrox expects a favourable business environment for the remainder of the financial year and into 2027, supported by robust growth in the semiconductor sector, continued investment in data centre infrastructure and rising demand for edge artificial intelligence (AI) devices.\n\nThe company — which makes machines used to automatically inspect and detect defects in semiconductor components and printed circuit board assemblies — said it is seeking to capture a slice of the increasing complexity of AI accelerators and high bandwidth memory.\n\nNet profit in the first nine months of the year also jumped to RM254.8 million from RM87 million a year earlier, supported by sustained capital expenditure deployment from strong AI infrastructure demand and electronics manufacturing customers.\n\nRevenue for the period also more than doubled to RM1.13 billion from RM552.7 million.\n\n“The group will continue to exercise prudent cost management and operational discipline to mitigate potential risks from foreign exchange volatility and geopolitical uncertainties,” ViTrox said."],"summary":"ViTrox Corporation Bhd (KL: VITROX) – November 2026 update\n\n- Latest quarterly results (3QFY2026): Net profit RM118.6 million, up from RM34.7 million a year ago; revenue RM485.1 million, up ~110% YoY. Volume growth drove lower unit costs.\n- Nine-months performance: Net profit RM254.8 million; revenue RM1.13 billion, both more than double from the prior year.\n- Outlook: Expects a favorable business environment into 2027, backed by robust semiconductor sector growth, continued data center capex, and rising demand for edge AI devices.\n- Strategic focus: Expanding presence in AI accelerators and high-bandwidth memory; leveraging AI infrastructure demand and electronics manufacturing customers.\n- Risks/mitigation: Emphasizes prudent cost management and operational discipline to address FX volatility and geopolitical uncertainties.\n\nRelevance to query: Aligns with 2026 November developments on ViTrox’s strong revenue/profit expansion amid AI, semiconductor inspection demand, and ongoing AI infrastructure investment.","image":"https://assets.theedgemarkets.com/Vitrox-1-APP-vitroxcom_4_2.jpg"},{"id":"https://industrialandland.com.my/news/vitrox-500000-sq-ft-batu-kawan-plant-campus-5.html","title":"ViTrox's 500,000 sq ft Batu Kawan plant to triple capacity | Your Industrial & Land Agent","url":"https://industrialandland.com.my/news/vitrox-500000-sq-ft-batu-kawan-plant-campus-5.html","publishedDate":"2026-11-09T22:22:39.000Z","author":"Scott Seow","text":"ViTrox's 500,000 sq ft Batu Kawan plant to triple capacity\n\n9 Nov 2026 · Expansion · 3 min read\n\n# ViTrox's 500,000 sq ft Batu Kawan plant to triple capacity\n\nScott Seow\n\nProbationary Estate Agent · PEA 4428 · CID Realtors Sdn Bhd\n\nEnlarge\n\nKey takeaways\n\n- ViTrox is building a five-storey, 500,000 sq ft plant in Batu Kawan, 3.3 times the 150,000 sq ft it makes machines in today\n- It should come on stream in about 15 months, and the first two floors may open earlier\n- CIMB puts the cost of \"Campus 5\" at RM150m–RM200m; ViTrox has not disclosed a site, contractor or cost\n- ViTrox owns 21 acres bought from PDC at RM52 psf in 2021 and has applied for more land\n\nViTrox Corporation Bhd is building a new five-storey manufacturing plant of 500,000 sq ft in Batu Kawan, Penang. That is more than three times the 150,000 sq ft it uses to make machines today.\n\nCo-founder and managing director Datuk Chu Jenn Weng told The Edge in September that the plant should come on stream in about 15 months. The first two floors may be used before the whole building is finished. He expects it to give the group at least three times its present capacity, with more gains from automation and AI.\n\n## Why ViTrox needs the space\n\nViTrox makes machines that inspect chips and circuit boards, and its factories are full. Revenue for the nine months to 30 September 2026 doubled to RM1.13 billion. Third-quarter revenue was a record RM485.1 million, driven by inspection systems for AI infrastructure and networking equipment, its Bursa filing shows.\n\nIts Batu Kawan campus already has about 924,000 sq ft of space, according to the 2025 annual report. Campus 2.0 was 92.4% in use at the end of 2025, and a further 105,775 sq ft of floor space was due to be renovated and in use by March 2026 to clear bottlenecks.\n\n## What the analysts say\n\n- Maybank IB (June 2026): ViTrox was running near maximum output, and a new facility was slated for the second half of 2026\n- CIMB Securities (August 2026): named a planned 500,000 sq ft manufacturing facility. As reported by Business Today, CIMB put the investment in the new \"Campus 5\" in Batu Kawan at RM150 million to RM200 million, with construction from the second half of 2026\n\nViTrox has not announced a building contract, site or cost for the plant on Bursa. The RM150m–RM200m is CIMB's figure.\n\n## The land ViTrox holds\n\nViTrox's 2025 annual report lists three titles in Batu Kawan Industrial Park, all on 60-year leases:\n\n- PT 5920, 22.2 acres: Campus 2.0 and 3.0 at 746 Persiaran Cassia Selatan 3, bought in 2014\n- PT 6145, 13.0 acres, and PT 6141, 8.1 acres: bought from the Penang Development Corporation (PDC) in May 2021 for RM48.3 million. The filing gives the price as RM52 psf, plus a charge for highway frontage\n\nThe report lists the 2021 land as vacant at the end of 2025, but part of it carries the ViTrox Institute of Technology (VIT). This is a five-storey, 166,300 sq ft training and research centre, built by South Island Building under a RM46 million contract awarded in July 2024. ViTrox planned to move in by October 2026.\n\nIn April, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said ViTrox had applied to PDC for more land in Batu Kawan. The Edge also reported that the group has plans for an innovation park and a bigger education hub, including a possible extra 50-acre site.\n\nNone of the filings or interviews says which plot the new plant will stand on.\n\n## A busy corner of Penang\n\nThe plant adds to a run of large builds in Batu Kawan. UWC has earmarked RM230 million for a 620,696 sq ft factory nearby. ViTrox was also among the 18 local test-equipment makers at the March workshop behind the planned Penang ATE Campus in Batu Kawan.\n\n📰 Sources\n\nscott@ (scott@industrialandland.com.my)\n\n- +6018-466 8066 (+60184668066)\n- WhatsApp\n- scott@industrialandland.com.my\n- Contact form","highlights":["# ViTrox's 500,000 sq ft Batu Kawan plant to triple capacity\n\nScott Seow\n\nProbationary Estate Agent · PEA 4428 · CID Realtors Sdn Bhd\n\nEnlarge\n\nKey takeaways\n\n- ViTrox is building a five-storey, 500,000 sq ft plant in Batu Kawan, 3.3 times the 150,000 sq ft it makes machines in today\n- It should come on stream in about 15 months, and the first two floors may open earlier\n- CIMB puts the cost of \"Campus 5\" at RM150m–RM200m; ViTrox has not disclosed a site, contractor or cost\n- ViTrox owns 21 acres bought from PDC at RM52 psf in 2021 and has applied for more land\n\nViTrox Corporation Bhd is building a new five-storey manufacturing plant of 500,000 sq ft in Batu Kawan, Penang. The RM150m–RM200m is CIMB's figure."],"summary":"ViTrox Corp Bhd is expanding with a new five-storey manufacturing campus of about 500,000 sq ft in Batu Kawan, Penang, more than triple its current 150,000 sq ft output. The project, dubbed potentially as “Campus 5,” is expected to come on stream in roughly 15 months, with the first two floors usable earlier. CIMB Securities estimates the investment at RM150 million to RM200 million, though ViTrox has not disclosed contract awards, site details, or costs. ViTrox already owns about 21 acres at Batu Kawan and has applied for additional land. The expansion aims to boost capacity and accelerate automation and AI-driven throughput, aligning with robust demand for semiconductor inspection systems amid AI infrastructure growth. In the nine months to 30 September 2026, ViTrox reported revenue of RM1.13 billion (doubling year-to-date) and a Q3 revenue of RM485.1 million, driven by inspection systems for AI and networking equipment. The Batu Kawan campus currently spans around 924,000 sq ft, with Campus 2.0 near full utilization and planned renovations to alleviate bottlenecks. Market notes from Maybank IB and CIMB Securities in 2026 indicated near-maximum output and a slated second-half 2026 start for the new facility. No site, contractor, or formal cost details have been disclosed in Bursa filings.","image":"https://industrialandland.com.my/images/news/vitrox-batu-kawan-500000-sq-ft-plant-campus-5.webp"}],"searchTime":5819.8,"costDollars":{"total":0.012,"search":{"neural":0.007},"summary":0.005},"warnings":[{"code":"IGNORED_FIELD","path":"/contents/highlights/highlightsPerUrl","message":"contents.highlights.highlightsPerUrl is no longer supported and is ignored.
